nytimes_articles.headline: Alcoa Says Profits Fell 70% in 3d Quarter
nytimes_articles.abstract: Aluminum Co of America reports 70 percent drop in third-quarter profits, to $68.4 million, compared with year ago; says revenues slipped 2 percent, to $3.2 billion; results reflect $65.5 million charge after taxes to pay for shrinking payroll by 2,900 workers and costs of strike at forging plant (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Film Festival Regrets
nytimes_articles.abstract: Stuart Klawans letter says selection committee for New York Film Festival, on which he served, did not reject a film by Leon Ichaso because he criticized Fidel Castro, as Ichaso maintains in Oct 2 article (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: RESULTS PLUS
Chilly Scenes From Lonely People's Lives
nytimes_articles.abstract: Andre Techine's exploration of unrequited love. Somber, penetrating.

nytimes_articles.headline: How Dole Fell
nytimes_articles.abstract: Frank Rich Op-Ed column says Bob Dole campaign is doomed because he has ignored the pollster Frank Luntz's prescriptions for a successful Republican campaign: avoid harsh ideological attacks, address the future, steer clear of abortion, play to Americans' hunger for a sense of community and, most important, make sure calls for tax cuts are linked to fiscally responsible spending cuts (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Cardinals' Eckersley Proves He Can Still Make a Difference
nytimes_articles.abstract: Article on pitcher Dennis Eckersley, who has recorded saves in both games in helping St Louis Cardinals take 2-0 lead in their three-of-five-game series with San Diego Padres (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Ex-Police Chief Sentenced
nytimes_articles.abstract: Robert A Spina, former Police Chief of West Orange, NJ, is sentenced to three years in prison for tipping off target of drug and child abuse investigation in 1991; Spina has also been charged with abusing his wife, Suzanne, and endangering their children, but Judge Harold W Fullilove has not set trial date on those charges (New Jersey Daily Briefing) (S)0

nytimes_articles.headline: Would-Be Judges Stalled
nytimes_articles.abstract: Faith S Hochberg, US Attorney for New Jersey, was nominated for Federal judgeship in November, but Senate adjourned on Oct 3 without confirming her and 27 other judicial candidates; Dan Maffei, spokesman for Sen Bill Bradley, a Democrat who nominated Hochberg to bench, complains that confirmation process has become more partisan; Jean Lopatto, spokeswoman for Senate Judiciary Committee, defends record of 104th Congress, saying that 73 of 105 nominees were confirmed (New Jersey Daily Briefing) (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Foes Take Steps To Cut Tension In West Bank
nytimes_articles.abstract: Palestinian policemen and Muslim clerics join efforts to prevent any disturbances in West Bank and Gaza Strip, and the Israeli Army moves tanks out of sight to reduce tensions; Israelis say they will soon reopen one of the crossings at Gaza for limited transport of goods; most Palestinians appear disappointed by the outcome of the Washington meeting at which they failed to win concessions from Israel; Sec of State Warren J Christopher plans to meet with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Yasir Arafat and attend opening of their talks on Israeli withdrawal from Hebron (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Eleanor Roosevelt Honored in Hometown Today
nytimes_articles.abstract: Statue honoring Eleanor Roosevelt to be dedicated in Riverside Park, NYC; Mrs Clinton plans to attend ceremony; statue is first of American woman ever commissioned for a New York City park; photos (L)

nytimes_articles.headline: In Bridgeport, Stopping Cars To Stop a Wave of Killings
nytimes_articles.abstract: Connecticut State Troopers have set up roadblocks at Interstate 95 exit ramps in Bridgeport in attempt to stamp down drug trade believed to be behind 10 killings in two weeks; map; photos (L)

nytimes_articles.headline: The Personal Care Business Has Outpaced the Demand
nytimes_articles.abstract: Analysts say 'personal care business' is deeply troubled corner of otherwise-healthy cosmetics industry; say too many companies scrambled to get into high-margin business selling fruity shampoos and water-based cosmetics, wreaking havoc by saturating it with new stores; now, many are teetering near financial disaster; Nature's Elements has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, and Garden Botanika, which went public in May, has seen its stock price plummet by two-thirds on disappointing sales news; graphs; photos (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Suspect Is Back in Jail
nytimes_articles.abstract: Anthony R Rivers of Bronx, NYC, who was freed on bail on Oct 3 after being jailed in death of Police Officer Vincent Guidice, is jailed again for not completing deal he had made with is bail bondsman that led to his release; Rivers was charged with criminally negligent homicide and assault after Guidice died on May 22 after falling on broken mirror while answering domestic violence call involving Rivers (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Perot Loses New Bid To Join the Debates
nytimes_articles.abstract: Federal appellate panel upholds lower-court ruling against Ross Perot in his bid to join the Presidential debates; FCC also rebuffs Perot's petition to force the big television networks to sell him extra prime-time slots for his half-hour commercials (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Genital Ritual Is Unyielding in Africa
nytimes_articles.abstract: Tradition of female genital cutting remains strong in much of Africa despite rising chorus of international condemnation, but some seeds of change are noted as the debate over the practice slowly moves into public arena; organizations have sprung up to combat the practice, but they are small, ill financed and must struggle within societies where men rule women's lives, and old people, including old women, rule the young; purpose of the cutting, which diminishes a woman's ability to experience sex ual pleasure, is to help insure a woman's fidelity to her husband and her family, and the practice knows no class or religious boundaries; photos; map (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Constitutional Reform
nytimes_articles.abstract: Letter from State Sen Richard A Dollinger urges a limited state constitutional convention to effect the reforms of the New York state legislature suggested in Sept 30 editorial (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Rogers Is the Enemy In His Own Backyard
nytimes_articles.abstract: New York Yankees' player Kenny Rogers, who lives two minutes from the Ballpark in Arlington, Tex, home of Texas Rangers, knows the Rangers do not like him anymore; as a Yankee, Rogers knows he is the enemy in the town that was his baseball home for first seven years of of his career; he knows he will be booed when he plays against Rangers in best-of-five playoff series (L)

nytimes_articles.abstract: Editorial welcomes decision by New York City Board of Education to review its guidelines on sexual harassment by students; says 6- and 7-year-old boys may behave in ways that are inappropriate and need correction without warranting the label 'sexual harassment'

nytimes_articles.headline: The Berlin and Brahms, Measuring Each Other
nytimes_articles.abstract: Alex Ross reviews Berlin Philharmonic under direction of Claudio Abbado at Carnegie Hall; Peter Serkin is piano soloist in an all-Brahams program (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: BUSINESS DIGEST
European Union Seeks To Protect Small Airlines
nytimes_articles.abstract: European Commission says it is considering fairer system for allocating times for airplanes to take off and land, in attempt to keep large airlines from abusing market dominance (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Dollar Recovers After Dropping On Weak Employment Report
nytimes_articles.abstract: Dollar is hurt initially by surprisingly weak employment report but eventually rises as stocks and bonds surge in belief that Federal Reserve would hold off raising interest rates (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Dow in Surge Near 6,000 Spurred by Report on Jobs
nytimes_articles.abstract: Dow Jones industrial average shoots toward 6,000-mark as weakening job market confirms slowing of economy; Dow rises 60.01 points to close at 5,992.86, and Standard & Poor's 500-stock index surpasses 700-mark for first time, closing at 701.46 (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Lasorda Has Angioplasty
nytimes_articles.abstract: Former Los Angeles Dodgers manager Tommy Lasorda is admitted to Centinela Hospital Medical Center, Inglewood, Calif, after eperiencing chest pains; doctors perform repeat angioplasty after artery that was operated on June 26 closed (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Mathematics Myths
New Zealand Settles Maori Land Claims
nytimes_articles.abstract: New Zealand agrees to settle Maori land claim for $117 million in land and cash; also agrees to restore some traditional fishing rights and recognize the original Maori names of 78 places on the island, along with their European names (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Boys and Girls Require (A) Equal Scores or (B) Equal Tests
nytimes_articles.abstract: Stuart Mark Gottlieb letter opposes College Board plan for changes in Preliminary Scholastic Assessment Test to improve girls' chances for winning National Merit Scholarships; drawing (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: COMPANY BRIEFS
nytimes_articles.abstract: Checkfree Corp sells its securities certificate and accounting software subsidiary to Sungard Data Systems Inc for $20 million (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Thomas Dygard, 65, Children's Author
nytimes_articles.abstract: Thomas J Dygard, author of sports novels for children and former reporter and editor, dies at age of 65 (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Charles P. Bean, 72; Physicist Analyzed Superconductivity
nytimes_articles.abstract: Charles P Bean, physicist known for his analyses of superconductivity and magnetism, dies at age of 72 (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: G.O.P.'s Good-Luck Charm
nytimes_articles.abstract: Republican Party operatives across US inoculate themselves against discouraging polls and apathetic voters by recalling New Jersey Gov Christine Todd Whitman's last-minute escape from what seemed sure defeat in 1993, largely on strength of pledge to slash taxes; Republicans say if it worked for Whitman, it can work for Bob Dole--at least in New Jersey, a swing state with an aversion to high taxes (New Jersey Daily Briefing) (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: In the End, How Will Cigar Be Remembered?
nytimes_articles.abstract: William C Rhoden's Sports of The Times column on race horse Cigar, who will run for final time in New York on Oct 5 in million-dollar Jockey Club Gold Cup at Belmont Park; Cigar's final race will be Breeders' Cup Classic on Oct 26; photo (L)ü

nytimes_articles.headline: City Hall Threatens Action if Time Warner Rejects Channel
nytimes_articles.abstract: New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani administration steps up pressure in its effort to persuade Time Warner Inc to carry Rupert Murdoch's Fox News Channel, 24-hour cable news channel in New York City; administration suggests that refusal by Time Warner could influence city panel that would be reviewing company's lucrative cable franchises next week; veiled warning comes after Time Warner on Oct 3 rebuffed request by administration to put news channel temporarily on one of five public-access cable stations controlled by the city (L)

nytimes_articles.headline: MCKESSON PLANS TO ADD FOXMEYER HEALTH UNIT
nytimes_articles.abstract: McKesson Corp says it will pay $400 milion to acquire ailing drug unit of Foxmeyer Health Corp; Foxmeyer placed its Foxmeyer Drug Co unit in Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in August (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: High Canada Aide Quits After Somalia Scandal
nytimes_articles.abstract: David Collette resigns as Canada's Minister of Defense one day after an army official testifies that top military officials altered documents to cover up responsibility for the beating death of a Somali teen-ager at the hands of Canadian peacekeeping troops in 1993; will be replaced by Doug Young, Human Resources Minister (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Corrections
At a Ceremony in Kenya, A Harsh Rite of Passage For a Brother and Sister
nytimes_articles.abstract: Samburu people of Kenya continue to circumcise their teen-age boys and cut the genitals of their teen-age girls; for boys this is a painful but important rite of passage, with few lasting complications, but some women are fighting for a change in the girls' rite, which they say not only deprives them of sexual pleasure but also creates medical problems during childbirth and sometimes even leads to death; the Samburu regard uncut women as unclean, promiscuous and immature; photo (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: A Dominican Leader Receives an Official Embrace
nytimes_articles.abstract: Leonel Fernandez Reyna, who came to US with his parents at age 7, returned to his native Dominican Republic as a teen-ager, became a lawyer and politician, returned to New York City this week for his first visit as President of Dominican Republic; he has returned with reception by city's political and economic elite; in last three day, he has addressed United Nations, hobnobbed with business people, was lauded by Mayor Rudolph Giuliani and was courted by three potential candidates for mayor; receiving attention that reflects growing clout of half million or so Dominican immigrants in the city; photo (L)

nytimes_articles.headline: Campaign Debate Gives Hartford An Opportunity to Promote Itself
nytimes_articles.abstract: Debate between Pres Clinton and Bob Dole in Hartford, Conn, is seen by many residents as a pivotal moment in the sun for a city whose economy has suffered from decline of insurance industry and the loss of major banks; city and the surrounding region are enthusiastic about the event; urban experts say negligible discussion of cities during the campaign stems from the declining role of the Federal Government in urban affairs and from the candidates' electoral strategies, which emphasize the suburban vote and make urban policy a risky topic (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: NEWS SUMMARY
Guilty of Lottery Kickbacks
nytimes_articles.abstract: J David Smith, former national sales manager for Gtech Corp, which has operated New Jersey's lottery since 1984, is convicted of taking kickbacks from consulting firm Benchmark Group Inc of Linwood, NJ; Federal grand jury returns split verdicts on owners of Benchmark, convicting Steven Dandrea of bribery, conspiracy and other charges, but acquitting Joseph LaPorta of same charges (New Jersey Daily Briefing) (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: A 'Gone With the Wind' In China, Without War
nytimes_articles.abstract: Gigolo in love with cousin, 1920's China. Never gripping but has sweep and color.

nytimes_articles.headline: In Milan, Trading In Suits For Chiffon
nytimes_articles.abstract: Amy M Spindler reviews show of women's fall fashions in Milan, Italy, featuring designs of Miuccia Prada and Tom Ford of Gucci, Giorgio Armani and Jil Sander; photos (L)

nytimes_articles.headline: Beliefs
nytimes_articles.abstract: Roman Catholic Archbishop Jean-Marie Cardinal Lustiger's mention of 'void' after life brings discussion about what Christians are supposed to believe and widespread assumptions about faith (L)è

nytimes_articles.headline: INSIDE
Daly Says He Still Drinks
nytimes_articles.abstract: PGA golfer John Daly, admitted alcoholic and former PGA Tour problem child, admits he is drinking again; says he is a 'social' drinker and that alcohol has not been reason the level of his play lately has been below his usual standards (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Bond Prices Surge as Drop in Payrolls Indicates No Rate Rises
nytimes_articles.abstract: Treasury prices surge after September employment report bolsters expectations that Federal Reserve would not raise interest rates this year; price of 30-year bond rises 1 1/32, to 100 2/32 (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: A Stolen Dali Drawing Resurfaces After 13 Years
nytimes_articles.abstract: Drawing by Spanish Surrealist Salvador Dali that was stolen 13 years ago is in police custody; sketch, worth about $150,000, was stolen in June 1983 at Salvador Dali Museum in St Petersburg, Fla; Anna Kisluck, director of Art Loss Register, company that maintains international database of 70,000 stolen artworks, says drawing came to light as result of call on Oct 3 from a New York City dealer alerted by potential buyer (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Bridgeport's Battle
Rangers Hope It's Their Turn to Rally
nytimes_articles.abstract: Texas Rangers, who will play New York Yankees in fourth game of American League Division Series, hope it will be their turn to rally like the Yankees in previous games and prolong series to Oct 6 late afternoon finale (M)
